messages:
Anna (oncall): quick handoff — saw a burst of p95 token latency + 429s from the kv-cache path starting ~22:10 UTC. Root cause looks like a thundering rewrite flood from a small customer causing redis evictions and thundering re-fetches.

incident-bot: Pager: CACHE-ALERT-503 triggered for service=kv-cache cluster=eu-west-1 at 22:11:08 UTC (page routed to #eng-oncall).

Anna (oncall): actions taken so far: reduced max-batch-size on frontend to 8 -> dropped write amplification, temporarily disabled prefix prefetching for embeddings encoder, and scaled the redis replica set by +2 pods (manual). Observed p95 drop from 1.6s -> 420ms for most routes.

Matt P: thanks — are there ongoing customer requests causing the spike? do we have a knob to throttle a single API key?

Anna (oncall): yes saw a single API key ~10k QPS for short window. I've applied a soft-rate-limit rule on that key (10k -> 2k) via the rate-limiter console: `POST /admin/keys/{key}/limits` payload applied. Keeping it for next 30m while we validate.

Julie: good call. can you paste the redis eviction logs?

Anna (oncall): pasted relevant snippet: ```
[22:10:42] evicting key user:12345:prefix_cache size=412MB free=88MB
[22:10:43] eviction_count=1023 keys_removed=512 policy=volatile-lru
[22:10:45] client_read 192.0.2.14 CONN=384 ops=12000/s
```

Kevin: note — this customer is on dedicated routing in eu-west-1 (tier=standard). we should notify CS after the shift. possible follow-up: suggest batching/ttl change on their side.

Ops Lead: primary/secondary for next shift?

Matt P: I'll be primary for the next 2 hours (23:00–01:00 UTC). Anna — you can hand off as secondary for the early morning?

Anna (oncall): yeah I'll remain secondary until 01:30 UTC. Key handoff points:
- runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction (see mitigation steps, quick rollback commands)
- playbook commands I used: ```sh
# scale redis replicas
kubectl -n infra scale statefulset/redis-eu --replicas=5
# disable prefix prefetching on frontend
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/frontend PREFETCH_PREFIX=false
```

Matt P: next steps for me: monitor p95 for 30m, watch evictions metric (`redis.evictions.total`) and rate-limiter logs for the key to ensure it doesn’t burst back. If evictions > 2000 in 10m, re-open bridge and consider temporary routing fallback to us-west.

Anna (oncall): customer impact summary to include in escalation if needed: small subset (~0.3% of calls) saw 5–15s latencies and some 503s for ~12 mins. No broad data loss.

Kevin: FYI I'll draft a short CS note if we keep the soft-limit for >1h. Add me to the thread if you escalate.

Matt P: marking two follow-ups: (1) Add defensive per-key burst protection to rate-limiter (owner: infra-backend), (2) add alert for sudden single-key QPS spikes (owner: monitoring). I'll create tickets.

incident-bot: Incident CACHE-ALERT-503 transitioned -> acknowledged by Matt P at 22:18:09 UTC.

Anna (oncall): leaving a checklist for whoever picks up next: 1) confirm soft-rate-limit still active, 2) check redis.evictions.total and free memory on leader, 3) confirm prefetch flag rolled back if stable, 4) inform CS if limit persists >1h.

Julie: thanks — I'll take ownership of the follow-up docs and add a short post-incident note to the runbook.

Matt P: handoff complete from my side. ping me if it blips back. :thumbsup:
